title: Wings Over the Atlantic
tagline: The skies were closed to women — until she flew through them.

scenes.text: Newfoundland, May 20, 1932. A red Lockheed Vega sits on Harbour Grace airfield. The pilot climbs in alone — no navigator, minimal radio. Amelia Earhart intends to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean. No woman has done it before. Tonight she follows Lindbergh's path — alone.

scenes.speaker: Amelia Earhart
scenes.text: Women must try to do things as men have tried. When they fail, their failure must be but a challenge to others. The most difficult thing is the decision to act. The rest is merely tenacity.

challenge.instruction: Earhart takes off from Harbour Grace as the sun goes down and will fly into the sunrise. Work out the hour on each side of the ocean.
challenge.fact: Earhart flew a single-engine Lockheed Vega 5B, painted red with gold trim. The same aeroplane now hangs in the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum in Washington.

scenes.text: The flight was harrowing. Ice formed on the wings and caused a spin. Her altimeter broke. Fire broke out near the exhaust manifold. She flew through storms for 14 hours and 56 minutes — and landed in a field in Northern Ireland.

scenes.speaker: Amelia Earhart
scenes.text: A farmer walked up to my plane. He said, 'Have you come far?' I said, 'From America.' The look on his face was worth everything.

challenge.instruction: Ice on the wings, a broken altimeter, flames at the exhaust. Ride the winds across the Atlantic and find land.
challenge.fact: In 1932, Earhart flew solo from Newfoundland to Northern Ireland in 14 hours 56 minutes — battling icing, storm turbulence, and a leaking fuel tank.

challenge.instruction: Earhart learned her trade in a yellow biplane called The Canary. Brace its wings so they hold, whatever the air throws at them.
challenge.fact: Earhart took her first flying lessons in January 1921 from Neta Snook, one of the first women aviators in California, and saved for months to buy a plane of her own.

challenge.instruction: She has landed in a pasture near Londonderry. Lay the cable that carries the news back to New York.
challenge.fact: Charles Lindbergh made the first solo transatlantic flight in 1927. Earhart was the first WOMAN to do so — in 1932, flying from Newfoundland to Northern Ireland in 14 hours 56 minutes. She also set the record for fastest transatlantic solo flight at that time.

challenge.instruction: 1937: Earhart sets out to circle the globe with Fred Noonan navigating. Take his star sights and fix the Electra's latitude, leg by leg.
challenge.fact: Earhart and Noonan vanished on 2 July 1937 near Howland Island in the central Pacific. The US Navy and Coast Guard mounted a vast search, but no trace of them was ever found.

scenes.speaker: Amelia Earhart
scenes.text: This time the whole board is judged at once. Deploy An Jung-geun, George Bernard Shaw and me, turn us public, then declare the Olympics: the highest public Strength on the board when the round ends takes the prize.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 6 · Global Competition. Deploy your Great People, Toggle Public on each, then start the Olympics and End Turn to win the round with the highest public Strength on the board.
challenge.fact: A Global Competition counts every public Great Person on the whole board; followers and face-down cards add nothing. It lasts one round, and the strongest player draws a reward: event cards, followers or a new Great Person.
